openItems.explanation: Hana Yilmaz (E-1015), Safety Manager, is coded 4904 Clerical Office, which covers office work, but the roster says the work is at the office and job sites. A person decides the class: 4900 if the site work is oversight or inspection only, with no supervising, manual labor, equipment or deliveries (the quarter's 480 hours would cost $124.46 more); otherwise the highest-rated class of the work exposed to, 0510, since the jobs include wood frame ones ($1,875.89 more).

The eight project managers and assistant project managers are reported in 4900 on the roster's flag that they do not directly supervise crews. 4900 also excludes anyone who does manual labor, operates or repairs equipment, or delivers supplies at a site, and the client's records do not say. A person confirms these duties with the controller.

Payroll took the employee share on one and a half hours for each overtime hour. L&I counts an overtime hour as one hour, and deducting more than the share is not allowed. Over-deducted in Q3: $504.52. The draft reports actual hours; a person arranges the refunds.

Tomas Arvelo has no contractor registration and no UBI on file, two of the seven conditions in RCW 51.08.181. A person checks L&I's contractor-registration lookup and the Department of Revenue's business lookup for Tomas Arvelo: if either is missing, the exclusion fails on the facts and the work is covered; if both exist, whether the work was free from the foreman's control is the judgment. If the work is covered, 504 hours at Tideflats Cold Storage belong in 0518: $1,189.24 of premium.

Unsigned draft. The report was due October 31, 2026, a Saturday, and L&I accepts a postmark of Monday, November 2; nothing has been filed or paid. L&I adds a penalty of 5% of the premium for the first month or part of a month late, then 10% and 20%, at least $10, plus 1% interest a month (see the rule checks). A person reviews, files and pays it.

rules.question: What must the quarterly report give L&I, and when does an unpaid premium become delinquent?
rules.whyItMatters: The statute sets what the report contains, the quarter's payroll and hours by class, and the day an unpaid premium becomes delinquent.
rules.effective: RCW 51.16.060 as published; last amended by 2022 c 281 s 12.
rules.excerpt: ... shall, on or before the last day of January, April, July and October of each year thereafter, furnish the department with a true and accurate payroll for the period in which workers were employed by it during the preceding calendar quarter, the total amount paid to such workers during such preceding calendar quarter, and a segregation of employment in the different classes established pursuant to this title ... Premiums for a calendar quarter, whether reported or not, shall become due and delinquent on the day immediately following the last day of the month following the calendar quarter.

rules.ruleOrLimit: By the last day of January, April, July and October, each employer reports the preceding quarter's payroll and hours by risk class and pays the premium.
